title: Wage War Against Comfort (Mental Health for the Modern Man)
summary: Filmed outdoors, NH argues that modern comforts (outrage media, social media, doom scrolling, cheap dopamine) make men miserable, and that the fix is to subtract them rather than add habits. He covers outsourcing personal responsibility, treating anxiety and sadness as signals and habits to manage, a circle of priorities from self outward, active gratitude, nature, and keeping training as the habit that holds dark thoughts at bay.
claims: Self-improvement should mostly mean subtracting modern comforts and habits that pile up as burdens, not adding more things like meditation routines
Audit the type of media you consume rather than just quitting platforms: the medium is neutral, but much content is engineered to make you mad or sad to keep you engaged
News media exploits the evolved bias toward negative information; consuming information you cannot use and that worsens your outlook is a net negative
Do not dodge real-life negativity, but do not import extra negativity from strangers online; it creates a cycle of desperation
Forums like 4chan are designed to make you angry and are not a source of information; he spent his teenage years there and never benefited
Algorithms both reinforce your beliefs and feed you deliberately abrasive opposite views because anger drives interaction; whoever can make you mad possesses you
Outrage-bait clips of women warp young men's view of the opposite sex; most men who say they hate women hate their online image, not real women
Stop clicking and sharing outrage content and thirst traps; for those creators all attention is good attention
Political content on social media makes you intellectually dishonest and convinces you that you have enemies, keeping you in fearful survival mode
Downloaded sadness about distant events you cannot affect leads to passivity; the world changes when people improve themselves first and then use that power
Claiming to live in the worst times outsources personal responsibility and teaches learned helplessness
Order your concern in circles: yourself first, then family, then community, then country, and the world last
Doom scrolling kills time and keeps you hyperstimulated so you never sit with your thoughts; boredom is a signal to work, read, hike or train
Consuming motivation content gives a dopamine spike that substitutes for actually acting, so people stay passive
You cannot kill the pleasure-seeking instinct; redirect it to delayed, earned pleasure like the endorphins after running, swimming or lifting
Effort must serve fulfillment and not become your whole identity; he fell into living to train rather than training to live (his gymcel phase)
Seek contentment by shrinking the list of things you think you need to be happy rather than ticking off accomplishments
Gratitude is an active daily habit, not a passive feeling
His mother taught him gratitude by making him list his limbs, blanket, roof, breakfast and warm school each morning, contrasting with his grandfather who worked in the mines at nine
Most people with mental health struggles are clinically normal; the problem is an environment lacking external struggle, especially for men who find meaning in struggle
Anxiety is a message that something needs to happen, usually action, rather than something to simply numb
Allow yourself a sad day instead of intellectualizing or running from it; avoiding small doses of emotion leaves you unable to cope with big ones
As a control freak he used to spiral for 48 hours or two weeks over small setbacks and fixed it by treating his reaction as a habit to work on
Emotions happen to you, but how you react and which habits you feed is your responsibility
Practice active gratitude with rituals that anchor you in the present, such as eating without screens and putting the phone away around people
Each morning in good health, say out loud that today is a good day because you are healthy
Spending 20 years in Paris left him chronically depressed; moving somewhere green made his mental health skyrocket
If you cannot get into nature, books are the healthiest escapism because they take effort and have no algorithm
Training is his rock: if he stops for three or four days the dark thoughts return, because the habit was what kept them at bay
Happiness is an act and contentment its result; you must keep up the habits that built it
